prs.title: fix: isolate streamable HTTP request errors
prs.author: he-yufeng
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Errors in the streamable HTTP transport are not propagated back to callers as JSONRPCError responses, causing tool calls to hang or loop indefinitely. All four PRs add the same fix pattern — catching a specific failure mode and sending a JSONRPCError back on `ctx.read_stream_writer` instead of silently returning or looping. #1578 catches connection death in `_handle_post_request`. #2395 catches reconnection exhaustion and sends an error instead of returning silently. #2613 replaces `response.raise_for_status()` with explicit status-code checking so HTTP 4xx/5xx become JSONRPCErrors. #2607 wraps the entire `handle_request_async` call in a try/except at the task level, which subsumes the cases covered by #1578 and #2613 (the exception raised by `raise_for_status()` would be caught here too). (4 PRs)

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same pickle-safety bug in `src/mcp/shared/exceptions.py` on the same base commit (`f153ea319d`): Python's default `__reduce_ex__` reconstructs exceptions by calling `cls(*self.args)`, but `MCPError` and `UrlElicitationRequiredError` store only a plain string in `self.args` (set by `super().__init__(error.message)`), causing a `TypeError` on unpickle because their constructors expect an `ErrorData` or `elicitations` list, not a bare string. (2 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2555 uses the standard Python pickle protocol by implementing `__reduce__` directly on the class, includes explicit test coverage in `tests/shared/test_exceptions.py`, and closes the tracked issue (#2431). PR #2478 introduces a module-level `_restore_mcp_error` dispatcher whose call-site (`__reduce__`) is not visible in its diff — the diff is incomplete — making it harder to evaluate coverage. #2555's approach is self-contained: the reconstruction logic lives on the class itself, and reconstructing from `(self._elicitations, self.message)` preserves the typed `elicitations` list rather than relying on the wire-format dict.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2744 uses an unconditional `str(uri) for uri in redirect_uris` conversion, which handles all URL subtypes (AnyUrl, AnyHttpUrl, etc.) without a guard. PR #2701's selective `str(uri) if isinstance(uri, AnyUrl) else uri` would leave non-AnyUrl non-string objects unconverted, making it a narrower fix. PR #2744 also positions the validator after the related `_empty_string_optional_url_to_none` method, keeping related validators grouped together.
